title: Transport and containment
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Any worker who transports kit, products and equipment between the store, the vehicle and sites in any Titan Academy business.
learningOutcomes: Contain each class of kit during transport so that nothing spills, mixes or moves.
Describe the containment measures for products, waste and wet items.
Identify the transport rules that must be checked before carrying dangerous goods.

instruction.heading: Contain by class
instruction.body: Each class of kit needs its own containment in transport. Products should be in sealed, labelled containers, upright, in a tray or bunded area where the vehicle has one, and separated by incompatibility. Waste should be in sealed bags or lidded bins. Wet cloths and mop heads should be in a separate bag so that water does not reach the products or the documents. Equipment should be secured so that it cannot move or fall. Documents should be kept dry and out of the way of spills, and copies of SDS should be available in the vehicle.

instruction.heading: Vehicle and driver practices
instruction.body: Secure the load with straps, racks or lockable boxes before driving. Keep chemicals out of the passenger cabin and keep the vehicle ventilated. Do not carry chemicals next to food or drink. Check the containers for leaks at the start of each day and after each stop. If a container leaks, stop, contain the leak as the SDS directs, ventilate the vehicle if safe, and report it.

instruction.heading: Dangerous goods
instruction.body: Some products and quantities are dangerous goods under transport rules. In Victoria, the vehicle licence limits for dangerous goods are set by quantity, as stated in the licence notice in this lesson. Check the product's classification and those limits before transporting any larger quantity, and do not transport a product that you have not confirmed as permitted.

procedure: Contain each class of kit separately, with sealed and labelled products upright and separated by incompatibility.
Bag and seal waste, and bag wet cloths separately from products and documents.
Secure all equipment and products with straps, racks or lockable boxes.
Check containers for leaks at the start of the day and after each stop.
If a leak occurs, contain it as the SDS directs and report it.
Confirm the dangerous goods position for any larger quantity before transport.

workedExamples.situation: A bucket of wet mop heads is placed in the vehicle on top of a box of product containers.
workedExamples.reasoning: Move the wet items to a separate bag in a separate position, so that water does not reach the products. Check the product containers for leaks, and secure the box so that it cannot slide.

equipmentAndPpe: Sealed bags for waste and wet items

commonErrors.error: Placing wet items in the same container as products or documents.
commonErrors.prevention: Bag wet items separately and keep them away from products and documents.

commonErrors.error: Carrying a leaking container because it is almost empty.
commonErrors.prevention: Check for leaks each day and contain or replace any leaking container.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Vehicle licence threshold (Victoria): a vehicle must be licensed for the class of dangerous goods it carries when the dangerous goods on the vehicle are in a receptacle with a capacity of more than 500 litres or 500 kilograms, or when the total capacity of all intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) holding dangerous goods on the vehicle is more than 3,000 litres. A prime mover of a semi-trailer or combination vehicle, and certain trailers, do not need a vehicle licence. This lesson does not grant a dangerous goods vehicle licence or any permit to transport dangerous goods.
SDS must be accessible at the workplace, as WorkSafe Victoria states for hazardous substances. Keeping SDS copies in the vehicle supports that duty when the vehicle is used for the work.

qualityStandard: Each class of kit is contained separately during transport.
No product is carried in the passenger cabin or next to food or drink.
Every leak is contained and reported.
documentationEvidence: Daily vehicle check record for leaks and load security.
Leak or spill record with the product, quantity and action taken.
summary: Contain products, waste, wet items and documents separately.
Secure the load and check for leaks each day and after each stop.
Confirm dangerous goods rules before carrying larger quantities.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should wet mop heads be placed in the vehicle?
options: On top of the product containers in the back of the van
In a separate sealed bag, away from products and documents.
In the passenger cabin with the windows closed and the door shut

knowledgeChecks.question: A product container is found leaking in the van. What is correct?
options: Keep driving to the job and deal with the leak at the job site
Wipe it with a cloth and put the cloth back in the kit today
Contain the leak as the SDS directs, ventilate if safe and report it.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say to check before transporting a larger quantity of a product?
options: Put it in the passenger cabin
Assume the limit is the same as the last trip
Check the product's classification and those limits
